# IBM Instana ↔ IBM NS1 Connect Integration

## Purpose

Automate DNS traffic steering (failover, geo-steering, load balancing) by wiring
IBM Instana health events directly into IBM NS1 Connect via webhooks. When an
Instana alert fires, NS1 instantly changes DNS answers — no human in the loop.

---

## Prerequisites

| Item | Where to get it |
|------|-----------------|
| IBM NS1 Connect account | https://my.nsone.net/ |
| NS1 API Key | NS1 portal → Settings → API Keys → Add Key |
| Instana tenant URL | Provided by your Instana administrator or SaaS invite |
| Instana user with Settings write access | Instana → Settings → Team Members |

---

## Step 1 — Configure NS1 (DNS zone + filter chain)

1. Log in to **https://my.nsone.net/**
2. Navigate to **DNS** tab → click **+** to add a new zone.
   - Domain name: `<your-domain>` (e.g. `app.example.com`)
   - Leave all other settings as default → **Save Zone**
3. Click **1 Record** next to the new zone → **Add record**
   - Record type: `CNAME`
   - Name: `<app-name>` (e.g. `replicated-app`)
   - TTL: `30`
   - Answer 1: `<primary-endpoint>`
   - Click **Add answer** → Answer 2: `<backup-endpoint>`
4. Click **Create Filter Chain** and add these filters (in order):
   - **Up** — marks answers as up/down
   - **Priority** — sets primary (1) vs backup (2)
   - **Select First N** — returns only the top available answer
5. Click **Priority** filter:
   - Primary endpoint → Priority `1`
   - Backup endpoint → Priority `2`

---

## Step 2 — Create an NS1 Data Feed (Webhook endpoint)

1. In the NS1 portal, navigate to **Integrations**.
2. Click **+** to add a new data feed:
   - Source type: **NS1 API**
   - Name & Label: `Instana-<app-name>` (e.g. `Instana-app-1`)
   - Click **Save feed**
3. **Copy the Feed URL** — you will paste this into Instana.
4. Go to **Settings → API Keys → Add Key** and copy your NS1 API key.

---

## Step 3 — Create the IBM NS1 Connect Alert Channel in Instana

> ℹ️ Instana now has a dedicated **IBM NS1 Connect** alert channel type
> (preferred over the generic webhook for new setups).

1. In Instana, go to **Settings → Global settings → Events & alerts → Alert channels**.
2. Click **Add alert channel** → select **IBM NS1 Connect** → **Add alert channel**.
3. Fill in the configuration fields:

   | Field | Value |
   |-------|-------|
   | **Name** | `NS1 Production DNS Failover` (or similar) |
   | **Webhook URL** | Paste the NS1 Feed URL from Step 2 (format: `https://api.nsone.net/v1/...`) |
   | **Custom HTTP Header — Key** | `X-NSONE-Key` |
   | **Custom HTTP Header — Value** | `<your-ns1-api-key>` |

4. Click **Create**.

> ⚠️ Note: The IBM NS1 Connect channel does **not** support the "Test Channel"
> button. You must trigger a real alert to verify delivery.

---

## Step 4 — Configure an Alert in Instana with Custom Payload

1. Navigate to **Settings → Events & Alerts → Alert Configurations**.
2. Click **New Alert Configuration** (or edit an existing one).
3. Fill in:
   - **Name**: e.g. `Disk Usage > 70% NS1 Failover`
   - **Alert on**: Events → select a relevant event (e.g. `Disk Usage > 70%`)
   - **Scope**: `All available entities` (or narrow to specific hosts/services)
4. Under **Alert Channels**, select the `NS1 Production DNS Failover` channel.
5. Under **Custom Payloads**, add:

   | Key | Value |
   |-----|-------|
   | `custom:up` | `0` |

6. Click **Create** (or **Save**).

---

## Step 5 — Wire the NS1 Filter to the Data Feed

1. In NS1, navigate back to your DNS zone and record.
2. Click on the **Up** filter in the filter chain.
3. For the **backup** answer: set value to `true` (always up).
4. For the **primary** answer:
   - Click the **Feed** icon (📡)
   - Select the `Instana-app-1` data feed you created in Step 2
5. Save.

Now when Instana sends `custom:up = 0` via the webhook, NS1 will mark the primary
answer as **down** and automatically route traffic to the backup endpoint.

---

## DNS Failover Behaviour

```
Instana alert fires
        │
        ▼
Webhook POST to NS1 Feed URL  (custom:up = 0)
        │
        ▼
NS1 Up filter marks primary answer = DOWN
        │
        ▼
NS1 serves backup endpoint for all DNS queries
        │
Instana alert manually closed  (custom:up = 1 or omitted)
        │
        ▼
Operator verifies primary is healthy → manually close alert in Instana
        │
        ▼
NS1 restores primary answer
```

> ⚠️ **Failback is intentionally manual** — this prevents automatic failback
> during transient outages and gives operators control over restoration timing.

---

## Verification Checklist

- [ ] NS1 DNS zone resolves correctly: `dig <app-name>.<domain>` returns primary endpoint
- [ ] NS1 data feed URL is reachable from Instana (no firewall blocks to `api.nsone.net`)
- [ ] Instana alert channel is created and shows **IBM NS1 Connect** type
- [ ] Trigger a test alert in Instana → check NS1 **webhook logs** (Integrations → your feed → Logs)
- [ ] `dig <app-name>.<domain>` now returns **backup** endpoint after alert fires
- [ ] Manually close the alert in Instana → primary endpoint restored in DNS

---

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---------|-------------|-----|
| No webhook logs in NS1 | Wrong feed URL in Instana | Re-copy the exact URL from NS1 Integrations |
| 401 Unauthorized in NS1 logs | Missing or wrong API key | Verify `X-NSONE-Key` header value |
| Primary not failing over | Up filter not connected to feed | Redo Step 5 — link feed to Up filter on primary answer |
| Failback not working | Alert not closed in Instana | Manually close the alert in Instana Events view |
| No test button available | Expected — NS1 Connect channel limitation | Trigger a real alert (e.g. raise a threshold temporarily) |
| Different payloads per zone | Not supported on one channel | Create separate alert channels + configurations per NS1 zone |

---

## Best Practices

1. **Use descriptive names** for alert channels and feeds (include environment: prod/staging).
2. **Set low TTL** (30s) on the DNS record so failover takes effect quickly.
3. **Configure multiple webhook URLs** in the channel for redundancy across NS1 regions.
4. **Test failover before going live** — trigger a real alert in a staging environment.
5. **Monitor NS1 webhook delivery logs** regularly to detect silent failures.
6. **Use manual failback** (do not auto-close alerts) for production traffic.
7. **Separate alert channels per use case** — one for failover, one for load balancing.
